Package hadur2.core.model

Class WaveManager

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.model.WaveManager
public class WaveManager extends Object
The waves in flight on one side of the duel, and the bookkeeping that decides when each one has passed its target.

The core keeps two. HadurCore's gun wave manager holds a wave from us at the enemy for every scan, real or virtual; when one breaks, the gun logs where the enemy went and scores the virtual guns. MoveController's holds a wave from the enemy at us for every scan; the one whose fire time matches a shot the energy ledger found becomes a firing wave (WAVE-1, WAVE-2), and only firing waves are surfed and, when they break, logged as where the enemy aimed. Waves are kept in the order they were added, which is fire-time order.

A wave can only be judged against the target's states during its flight, and scans do not arrive every tick. So every scan's target state is added to a per-wave RobotStateLog, and when the wave is gone the log fills in the missing ticks by interpolation to recover every tick on which the wave was crossing the target. That log is dropped with its wave, so it holds at most one wave's flight (RES-2); the list itself is cleared each round.

    • checkActiveWaves

      public void checkActiveWaves(long currentTime, RobotState lastScanState, WaveManager.WaveBreakListener listener)
      Advances every wave to currentTime: records the target's state in each wave's log, and hands each wave that has now completely passed the target to listener, with the states during which it was crossing the target, before removing it.
      Parameters:
      currentTime - the current tick
      lastScanState - the target's latest state; nothing happens unless it is from currentTime
      listener - told about each wave that broke, once

    • getWaveBreakStates

      List<RobotState> getWaveBreakStates(Wave w, long currentTime)
      The target's states, one per tick from the wave's fire time to the tick before currentTime, on which the wave was breaking (touching the target's box): Wave.WavePosition.BREAKING_FRONT or Wave.WavePosition.BREAKING_CENTER. Unobserved ticks are interpolated from the wave's log; ticks that cannot be are left out. These are the states Wave.preciseIntersection(java.util.List<hadur2.core.model.RobotState>) turns into the range of firing angles that would have hit.

    • findClosestWave

      public Wave findClosestWave(Point2D.Double targetLocation, long currentTime, boolean onlyFiring, String botName, double bulletPower)
      The wave most likely to have carried a bullet seen at targetLocation: of the waves that pass the filters, the one whose front at currentTime is nearest the bullet, within 50 pixels (WAVE_MATCH_THRESHOLD). The core uses it to tie a bullet that hit us, or hit one of ours, back to the enemy wave that fired it.
      Parameters:
      targetLocation - where the bullet was, pixels
      currentTime - the current tick
      onlyFiring - whether to consider firing waves only
      botName - the firer's name; null or empty matches any
      bulletPower - the bullet's power, matched to within 0.001; -1 matches any
      Returns:
      the closest wave, or null when none is within the threshold

    • findSurfableWave

      public Wave findSurfableWave(int surfIndex, RobotState targetState, Wave.WavePosition unsurfablePosition)
      The surfIndex-th wave (0 = the oldest) that is still worth dodging: a firing wave whose bullet has not already hit us or been shot down, and which has not reached unsurfablePosition relative to targetState. The surf asks with Wave.WavePosition.BREAKING_CENTER, so it stops dodging a wave once the wave is past our centre and turns to the next one.
      Parameters:
      surfIndex - which surfable wave, counting from the oldest
      targetState - our state, usually now or predicted
      unsurfablePosition - the first position at which a wave is no longer surfable
      Returns:
      the wave, or null when there are not that many surfable waves
